chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflection in agents, comprising three stages. First, Environment Reflection Skill Discovery (RSD) injects grounded tool-feedback perturbations into environment scaling, samples a capability-diverse LLM pool, mines matched success-failure pairs, and summarizes reusable reflection meta-skills. Building on this skill library, Reflective Supervised Fine-Tuning (ReSFT) converts each skill into supervision for self-reflection, skill recovery, and user-centric correction. Finally, On-Policy Reflective Policy Optimization (ORPO) combines agentic reinforcement learning under noisy interactions with reflection-guided on-policy distillation to further elicit proactive reflection.
chk_method.reason: The poster describes the three-stage Agent-Reflex framework (RSD, ReSFT, ORPO) and their functions, matching the reference.

The final corpus contains 54K trajectories, merging verified Qwen3-8B successes with SR, KR, and UR samples.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: We present Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflective thinking in agents. RSD mines reusable reflection meta-skills from matched success–failure trajectories under grounded tool-feedback perturbations. Building on this skill library, ReSFT turns each skill into complementary supervision for self-reflection, skill recovery, and user-centric correction, and ORPO further elicits proactive reflection by combining agentic reinforcement learning under noisy interaction with reflection-guided on-policy distillation. Across six challenging agent benchmark suites, Agent-Reflex improves long-horizon tool use and robustness under tool and user noise with stable training dynamics, supporting scalable agent training.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: The skill library is mined offline from a fixed snapshot of executable environments, so interface or dynamics changes may require periodic re-mining. Future work will investigate online skill summarization and incremental updating across larger, more diverse environment collections, extend the failure taxonomy to temporal signatures (latency, concurrency, partial writes), and distill richer privileged artifacts such as verified sub-plans or tool contracts with the same estimator.
